name: Slow Roasted Lemon Garlic Chicken
pitch: You've got the two stars of this dish — chicken and garlic — and a squeeze of lemon (or a splash of vinegar) is all you need to round it out.
steps: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Season the chicken generously inside and out with salt and pepper.
Break your garlic into cloves — no need to peel them. Tuck about two-thirds inside the chicken cavity and scatter the rest in the bottom of a roasting tin. Sit the chicken on top.
No lemon? No problem — drizzle a tablespoon of white wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar over the chicken and rub it in. Then drizzle with olive oil.
Roast at 220°C for 30 minutes to get the skin going, then drop the heat to 160°C (325°F) and let it slow-roast for at least 3–4 more hours. The meat will be fall-off-the-bone tender.
While the chicken rests (10–15 min), quickly wilt your spinach in a hot pan with a little oil and a pinch of garlic from the roasting tin. Serve the chicken right on top.

name: Quick Roast Chicken with Garlic
pitch: This weeknight roast comes together fast — your chicken and garlic do most of the work, and a few easy swaps cover the rest.
steps: Heat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Pat the chicken dry with paper towels — this is the secret to crispy skin.
Mix softened butter (or just olive oil if that's easier) with your garlic — minced or roughly crushed — and push it under the chicken skin with your fingers. Season all over with salt and pepper.
No lemon? A small splash of white wine vinegar or just some extra olive oil in the pan works fine. No thyme? Skip it or use any dried herb you have — oregano or rosemary are both great.
Roast at 220°C for 10 minutes, then turn the heat down to 180°C (350°F) and cook another 25–35 minutes depending on size. Juices should run clear when you poke the thickest part of the thigh.
Rest the chicken for 10 minutes before cutting in. While it rests, wilt your spinach in the same roasting pan on the stovetop with a little of the chicken drippings — easiest side dish ever.

name: Garlicky Spinach and Chicken with Goat Cheese
pitch: Skip the lamb and use your chicken instead — the real magic here is the wilted garlicky spinach, which is already halfway to dinner with what you have.
steps: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add your garlic (minced or sliced) and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the spinach and toss until just wilted, about 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Cook your chicken in the same pan — slice it into cutlets or use whatever form it's in. If it's already cooked, just warm it through with a little olive oil and seasoning.
No goat cheese? Crumbled feta works great, or just a dollop of cream cheese if that's what you've got. Even a fried egg on top would be satisfying here.
Serve the chicken over the garlicky spinach with your cheese crumbled on top. Simple, but genuinely good.
